newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Telecom says it, ITJ aiming for merger pact.
newsitem.headline: Japan Telecom says it, ITJ aiming for merger pact.

text.p: Japan Telecom Co Ltd said on Wednesday that it and International Telecom Japan Inc (ITJ) are negotiating a possible merger and aim to reach agreement by the end of March.
If they reach an agreement by the end of this month, the two companies would merge around October this year, Japan Telecom Vice President Haruo Murakami told a news conference.
Japan Telecom would remain in existence if they merge, he said.
Japan Telecom is one of Japan's domestic long-distance carriers and ITJ is one of the nation's international telecommunications companies.

Separately, ITJ confirmed the merger talks and that the companies are seeking to reach an agreement by the end of this month. But it added in a statement that specifics, such as a merger ratio, had not been decided so there was nothing to announce at the moment.
A ITJ spokeswoman said she could not provide further details.
Japan Telecom's Murakami said that Japan Telecom hoped to tie up with international telecommunications carrier Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co Ltd (KDD) in the future.

He added that Japan Telecom also hoped to tie up with TTNet, an affiliate of Japan's electric power firms, which offers a leased telecommunications line service and hopes to start a city call service in Tokyo.
It also hopes for a tie up with one of the three large international telecommunications consortia, such as the British Telecommunications Plc-MCI Communications Corp alliance Concert, Murakami said.
He said, however, that no decision on a possible partner had been made.

Murakami said that the merger was being considered because Japan Telecom thought it would be difficult to survive as the industry becomes more competitive if it operates only domestic long-distance services.
He also said that the company considered other telecoms companies as a possible merger partner but decided on ITJ because they had common shareholders.
"If we consider our future operations, it will be easier to get support from shareholders (for the merger) as we have common shareholders," Murakami said.
Murakami added the formal merger talks with ITJ started on March 5.
